# Optivus

> Optivus is a Canadian fractional CMO practice founded by Dean Reid, based in Cochrane, Alberta. It helps B2B companies in the $15M to $60M revenue range, including PE-backed portfolio companies, build go-to-market strategy, demand generation, and AI-ready marketing operations. Dean Reid has 25+ years of VP and Director-level marketing leadership at TELUS, Bell Canada, SMART Technologies, Veriforce, Userful, and TEC Canada.

All articles are written by Dean Reid. Statistics link to their original sources. Content may be quoted with attribution to Dean Reid, Optivus, and a link to the source page.

## Intelligence Series: essays

- [The 10-Point Go-To-Market Leak Finder](https://www.optivusprof.ca/gtm-leak-finder.html): Answers "Where does revenue leak in a B2B go-to-market funnel?" Revenue usually leaks in ten places that sit in different dashboards: speed to first response, lead qualification clarity, pipeline coverage, win rate by segment, sales cycle length, CAC payback, content distinctiveness, AI answer engine visibility, martech data readiness, and post-sale retention. Compare each against its benchmark, fix the cheapest leak first, and put one person in charge of all ten numbers.
- [The AI Convergence Trap: Why AI Is Making Every B2B Brand Sound the Same](https://www.optivusprof.ca/ai-convergence-trap.html): Answers "Why does AI make B2B content sound the same?" Because every vendor in a category now uses the same few AI models, trained the same way and prompted with the same playbook. Researchers call the result isomorphism: companies converge without anyone copying anyone. Default AI training measurably reduces language diversity, and polished writing no longer signals expertise, so buyers shift their trust to third-party proof such as reviews and citations.
- [The Cost of Inaction: How 12-Month Blind Spots Hand Market Share to Agile Competitors](https://www.optivusprof.ca/cost-of-inaction.html): Answers "What is the cost of inaction in B2B strategy?" The cost of inaction is the market position a competitor builds while your leadership team is still deciding. A 12-month delay in a strategic pivot typically means missing the first procurement cycle after a market shift, and with it the reference customers, implementation partnerships, and buyer preference that decide competitive structure for years. Lost revenue is the smallest part of the cost.
- [AI Theater vs. AI Architecture: What B2B Leaders Get Wrong About AI-Driven Revenue](https://www.optivusprof.ca/ai-theater-vs-ai-architecture.html): Answers "What is the difference between AI theater and AI architecture in B2B marketing?" AI theater is deploying AI tools without a strategy that connects them to revenue: more content and activity, but no movement in pipeline. AI architecture rebuilds the commercial operation so AI is embedded in the workflows that produce pipeline, including ICP refinement, content, lead scoring, and reporting, with a governance framework the CFO and board can trust.
- [Marketing Is a Financial Discipline, Not a Creative Exercise](https://www.optivusprof.ca/marketing-is-a-financial-discipline.html): Answers "Why should B2B marketing be treated as a financial discipline?" Because marketing’s job is to manufacture qualified demand, so it should be held to a pipeline number the way sales is held to a revenue number. Most B2B marketing fails not from incompetence but because teams are rewarded for activity such as posts, webinars, and open rates. Treating marketing as a financial function ties every activity to marketing-sourced pipeline and cost per opportunity.
- [What a Board Actually Needs From Marketing (It Is Not a Dashboard)](https://www.optivusprof.ca/what-a-board-needs-from-marketing.html): Answers "What does a board actually need from marketing?" An independent, audit-grade view of the revenue engine, not a dashboard. Most B2B boards have deep financial expertise but nobody who can challenge marketing’s numbers. A board-level growth advisor provides independent oversight of GTM strategy, demand generation, ICP, sales and marketing alignment, and attribution, and finds the gaps before an acquirer’s due diligence does.
- [Why B2B Executive Silence Is a Commercial Risk](https://www.optivusprof.ca/why-b2b-executive-silence-is-a-commercial-risk.html): Answers "Why is executive silence a commercial risk for B2B companies?" Because in a crowded B2B market, the executive who defines the problem owns the category. If your leaders aren’t visibly articulating your buyers’ problems with specificity and authority, competitors define them for you. Real thought leadership is a consistent, opinionated point of view from a named expert over 12 to 24 months, and it’s also what AI engines choose to cite.
- [Why 90% of Revenue Architects Are Competing on Price, and How to Stop](https://www.optivusprof.ca/why-revenue-architects-compete-on-price.html): Answers "How should a fractional CMO avoid competing on price?" By positioning on a specific, unfair advantage instead of on being cheaper than a full-time hire. Most fractional CMOs (Revenue Architects) pitch senior leadership at a fraction of the cost, which invites buyers to compare day rates. The stronger move is to own one of three positions: GTM governance architect, AI-native revenue engine builder, or exit-ready commercial advisor, each backed by measurable proof.
- [Why We Don’t Gate Our Thinking (And Why That Is the Point)](https://www.optivusprof.ca/why-we-dont-gate-our-thinking.html): Answers "Should B2B professional services firms gate their content?" Usually not. Gated content produces email addresses, while ungated content produces authority. For professional services, the product is the judgment of a specific person, which is best demonstrated by publishing real frameworks, diagnostic tools, and original perspectives openly. Buyers who understand your method before they call are already sold, and AI engines can only cite content they can read.
- [Stop Looking in the Mirror: Why Your Internal Strategy Audit Is Failing Your Market Position](https://www.optivusprof.ca/stop-looking-in-the-mirror.html): Answers "Why do internal strategy audits fail?" Internal strategy audits fail because they measure how well a company executes its current plan, not whether that plan still fits the market. They are run by the people who built the plan, using lagging internal metrics. The gaps that matter most, in positioning, competitive differentiation, and buyer perception, are only visible from outside, through buyer interviews and external research.
- [Death of the Click: Why AI Citations Are the New SEO](https://www.optivusprof.ca/death-of-the-click-ai-citations.html): Answers "Why are AI citations replacing SEO rankings?" Because AI-generated answers now resolve many searches on the results screen. Pew Research found people clicked through to a website in 8% of visits when a Google AI summary appeared, versus 15% without one. Visibility now depends on whether the AI names you as a source inside its answer, and cited brands see about 35% higher organic click-through rates.
- [Why 90% of B2B Marketing Strategy Is Just Performance Theater](https://www.optivusprof.ca/why-90-percent-b2b-marketing-is-performance-theater.html): Answers "What is performance theater in B2B marketing?" Performance theater is any marketing activity that produces metrics without producing qualified pipeline: content calendars, social posts, impressions dashboards, and agency reports that look busy but can’t be traced to a sales conversation. The test is one question: where did this quarter’s sales qualified leads come from? Real B2B marketing replaces it with expert attribution, proprietary research, and content clusters.
- [Why PE-Backed Companies Stall at $20M](https://www.optivusprof.ca/why-pe-backed-companies-stall-at-20m.html): Answers "Why do PE-backed companies stall at $20M in revenue?" Most PE-backed B2B companies stall around $20M because they grew on founder relationships and referrals, and that founder-led selling has a ceiling. Sponsors professionalize finance, operations, and HR, but rarely build the marketing infrastructure that manufactures qualified demand at scale: a defined ICP, sharp positioning, a demand engine, and pipeline measurement. The fix is a go-to-market architecture rebuild, not more sales headcount.

## Playbooks

- [Account-Based Marketing: A Strategic Growth Playbook for High-Value B2B Accounts](https://www.optivusprof.ca/account-based-marketing-playbook.html): Answers "What is account-based marketing, and how do you run it?" Account-based marketing (ABM) is a B2B strategy where sales and marketing jointly target a defined list of high-value accounts with personalized campaigns. Run it in four steps: co-create a joint ABM playbook with sales, map each account’s buying committee, personalize content by role and account tier, and govern the program with clear ownership, shared metrics, and quarterly reviews.
- [The Content Blueprint for High-Impact Demand Generation](https://www.optivusprof.ca/content-blueprint-demand-generation.html): Answers "What content should B2B companies create at each stage of the funnel?" At the top of the funnel (TOFU), publish educational blog posts, short videos, infographics, and SEO content. In the middle (MOFU), use case studies, webinars, comparison guides, and interactive tools. At the bottom (BOFU), offer demos, free trials, testimonials, and transparent pricing. After purchase, use onboarding, customer webinars, communities, and referral programs to drive retention and advocacy.
- [Building a Scalable Marketing Engine: The 5-Phase Playbook](https://www.optivusprof.ca/scalable-marketing-engine-playbook.html): Answers "How do you build a scalable B2B marketing engine?" Build it in five connected phases. First, research the market, competitors, and customers. Second, define positioning, messaging, and strategic plays. Third, plan the go-to-market: channels, calendar, funnel stages, and budget. Fourth, launch multi-channel campaigns with sales. Fifth, optimize through attribution, testing, and feedback loops. Each phase ends in concrete deliverables that feed the next.
- [The B2B SEO and AI Search Playbook: How to Get Found and Cited Without Ad Spend](https://www.optivusprof.ca/seo-playbook.html): Answers "How can a B2B company rank in Google and get cited by AI search without paid ads?" Work five pillars in order of leverage. Build a fast, well-structured technical foundation with schema markup. Earn external authority from directories, expert-source platforms, and guest publishing. Publish topic clusters written answer-first. Win local search with Google Business Profile and consistent listings. Then build a verifiable expert presence on LinkedIn, podcasts, the press, and community sites that AI engines trust, and measure both rankings and AI citations.
